newsitem.title: USA: B.A.T may weigh tobacco litigation pact-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T may weigh tobacco litigation pact-WSJ.

text.p: B.A.T Industries has indicated for the first time that it might consider an industrywide settlement to end tobacco-liability litigation in the United States, the Wall Street Journal said Thursday.

Company chief executive Martin Broughton said in a BBC television broadcast this week that B.A.T might weigh "some kind of payment to somebody," but that any pact would have to include immunity from future litigation, the report said.
A spokesman for B.A.T told the paper that Broughton's remarks should not be interpreted to mean that such a settlement will ever be reached.

"What it reflects is a shift in the industry's position from, 'We would never settle,' to 'Well, you know, maybe on the right terms it might be in our shareholders' interest to do so'," spokesman Michael Prideaux told the paper.

The report quoted Prideaux as saying that the right terms would include "not only an acceptable price, but immunity from all kinds of future liability suits" and that any pact would have to be industrywide.
